occasions.moment: the 4pm dip at a desk — hungry, flagging, two hours from dinner
occasions.competes_with: biscuits from the office jar, a chocolate bar, samosa/vada from the canteen, chai, a banana, or skipping it entirely
occasions.decided_by: speed, taste, what is within arm's reach, mild guilt
occasions.channel: office pantry, vending machine, the desk drawer stocked on Blinkit

occasions.moment: 11pm, scrolling in bed, wants something sweet
occasions.competes_with: chocolate, ice cream, leftover mithai, biscuits, nothing
occasions.decided_by: craving, what is in the fridge, 10-minute delivery
occasions.channel: Blinkit / Zepto / Instamart, the kitchen cupboard

occasions.moment: straight after the gym, 45 minutes before a proper meal
occasions.competes_with: a whey shake, eggs, a banana, dal-chawal at home, nothing
occasions.decided_by: protein per serving, habit, what the trainer said
occasions.channel: gym counter, HealthKart, Amazon, the gym bag

occasions.moment: leaving the house late, will not sit down to eat
occasions.competes_with: toast, poha, cereal, a bought sandwich, coffee alone, skipping
occasions.decided_by: one hand, no crumbs, keeps until 11am
occasions.channel: kitchen counter, the metro station kiosk, monthly grocery order

occasions.moment: a weekend or a bad day — wants a treat but not to feel bad about it
occasions.competes_with: dark chocolate, a 'healthy' dessert, regular chocolate anyway, fruit
occasions.decided_by: permission — whether it reads as a treat or as a compromise
occasions.channel: quick commerce, the supermarket aisle, a cafe

occasions.moment: airport, long drive, or a two-hour commute with no real meal in sight
occasions.competes_with: airport sandwich, chips, nuts, a Snickers at the counter, nothing
occasions.decided_by: portability, shelf life, what the counter is selling
occasions.channel: airport store, highway stop, petrol pump, packed from home

occasions.moment: a standing daily habit someone has decided to keep
occasions.competes_with: a powder, gummies, a multivitamin, real food, nothing
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it is working, cost per day
occasions.channel: Amazon subscribe, HealthKart, the pharmacy, D2C

occasions.moment: the monthly or weekly shop — buying for other people as well as themselves
occasions.competes_with: biscuit packs, namkeen, cereal, whatever the kids will eat
occasions.decided_by: price per unit, family acceptance, keeps in the cupboard

everyday_alternatives: Cadbury Dairy Milk — ₹10 to ₹100 depending on size; the default sweet thing
Snickers — ~₹40 for 50g; the 'it's basically food' bar at the counter
Britannia Good Day, Marie Gold, 50-50, Bourbon — ₹10-₹40 biscuit packs
Parle-G — ₹5-₹10; the floor of the category
Sunfeast Dark Fantasy — ~₹30; the indulgent biscuit
Lay's / Kurkure / Bingo — ₹20 chips and namkeen
Haldiram's namkeen — ₹20-₹50 packs, and the household tin
Amul / Kwality Walls ice cream — ₹40-₹80 for the late-night version
canteen samosa, vada pav, or chai — ₹10-₹25, hot and immediate
a banana or an apple from the fruit cart — ₹10-₹20
leftover mithai in the fridge after any festival
nothing at all — waiting it out until the next meal

raw.label: loyalist_kitkat_break_ritual
raw.l1_context: Never came to it as nutrition at all — the afternoon tea break with the shift mates has had the same wafer bar in it for years.
raw.l2_category: Buys a single bar at the shop near the gate four or five afternoons a week, always the same coin price, always with cutting chai.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows which shops keep the bar cold and which sell stale stock. Does NOT know what whey is or that protein bars exist as a shelf. Does NOT read the back of any pack.
raw.l4_stance: Wants the same taste for the same coin at the same time. Rejects anything that has to be ordered in advance or comes in a box of eight.
raw.l5_behavior: Grabbed a KitKat at the kirana on the way back from the gate at 4, ate it standing with chai, put it on the running tab.

raw.label: switcher_canteen_samosa_swap
raw.l1_context: Fried canteen snack every afternoon started showing up as acidity and a heavy 5pm, so he began rotating whatever the drawer had instead.
raw.l2_category: Stocks the desk drawer on a ten-minute app once a fortnight; moves between namkeen packs, a protein bar box, and chips depending on mood.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows the drawer gets raided and cheap packs vanish first. Does NOT know whether the protein figure on a bar is verified. Does NOT know the difference between whey isolate and concentrate.
raw.l4_stance: Wants something that holds until dinner and does not smell up the desk. Rejects any bar that tastes chalky — he will not finish a box out of loyalty.
raw.l5_behavior: Added a RiteBite Max Protein bar to a Blinkit top-up alongside Lay's, ate the bar Tuesday and the chips Wednesday.

raw.label: upgrader_bournville_desk_drawer
raw.l1_context: A blood-sugar number on last year's company health check made him stop the two-biscuit-with-chai habit and look for a smaller, darker afternoon thing.
raw.l2_category: Keeps his own bar in a locked drawer, orders on a ten-minute app monthly, sticks to darker chocolate and one squares-not-bars rule.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows dark tastes less sweet and that he eats less of it. Does NOT know how much sugar is actually in what he switched to. Does NOT know what a protein bar costs or where singles are sold.
raw.l4_stance: Wants a small grown-up treat that does not read as kids' food. Rejects pastel wellness packaging and anything with a cartoon or a percentage shouted on the front.
raw.l5_behavior: Ordered Bournville on Zepto with the tea packet, broke two squares at 4.15 and left the rest in the drawer.
